Waseem is a writer here at GameRant. He can still feel the pain of Harry Du Bois in Disco Elysium, the confusion of Alan Wake in the Remedy Connected Universe, the force of Ken's shoryukens and the bizareness of every side story of the Yakuza series. He will play anything as long as it's got something unique and original about it, though he's still yet to dip his toes into multiplayer battle arena games like Dota 2. In his roles, he has applied the latest tools and workflows for project management, content creation, software development, and corporate risk evaluation. One of his biggest achievements has been building management-level dashboards and delivering regular data analysis to help keep an organization’s security posture strong and continuously improving. In addition, he has worked with GameRant for over 3 years, authoring nearly 1,000 articles across a wide range of video game genres.
Some of my favorite games include Elden Ring , Disco Elysium , and Alan Wake 2 , all for very different reasons. Elden Ring delivers one of the most rewarding open-world experiences I have ever played. I also have a special appreciation for the Resident Evil , Street Fighter , and Yakuza series. Resident Evil has consistently provided some of my best horror experiences. I have a lot of characters on Master Rank on Street Fighter 6, and even though I can take them one step further, I haven't played the game much in the past year.
Obtaining my first platinum after hours of grinding the True Final Millennium Tower in Yakuza 7. Beating Shin Amon through all the sweat and tears I could withstand in a gaming session seriously made me put the controller down in a huge sigh of relief. What a fight.
Xbox 360, something nostalgic about it. Still can't forget the days of playing co-op Gears of War with my brother or diving into a multiplayer Halo game online. Xbox, if you're listening, please bring back couch co-op games! With how many hours I have on the PS5 now, that is now my 2nd favorite!
